From Bavaria, a carpenter, who taught the trade to his son Kasper.
He landed at New York from Bremen on the Columbia on 30 September 1853: the list has Caspar Schmidt,
50, a Bavarian carpenter bound for Ohio, followed by eight younger Schmidts, very probably his children.
His wife Anna is not on it, so she may have crossed separately.
They lived in Seneca County, Ohio, then near Freeport, Illinois, and from 1860 in Barclay Township,
Black Hawk County, Iowa, where the 1878 directory has him on section 4.
His son Kasper helped build Barclay’s first Catholic church.
Her stone at Saint Francis Cemetery, Dunkerton, Iowa, is lettered in German: “Anna,
Frau von Casper Schmitt.” She died on 21 September 1883, aged 77 years, 8 months and 13 days,
which puts her birth at about 8 January 1806.
